C-VERDICT-EVIDENCE.Summary: Bind the review Verdict so it cannot stand in for a review that never ran. gate verdict re-runs ngrace review for the named change, persists that finding set onto the Verdict, and records explicit Ack children against specific finding identities. Apply refuses an unbound pass, a digest mismatch, an Ack that does not match the persisted set, and outcome fail. GateId stays closed. ngrace review stays read-only. A scope-breach finding is acknowledgeable; process-integrity failures of the close are not.

Goals.Goal: A pass Verdict recorded at close is bound to a tool-generated snapshot of ngrace review for that change: persisted Finding children plus a snapshotDigest, and one Ack child per persisted finding that names that finding's identity. Future audits read the Verdict, not a recomputed review.

Apply refuses when that binding is missing or false: unbound pass, digest mismatch, Ack of an id not in the persisted set, or outcome fail. unable-to-determine with host-capability-missing stays on the existing gateFailOn path.

The examining party (detached reviewer where the host allows it, otherwise the operator) records the bound verdict. The implementing executor does not. Skills state that split. The CLI does not claim to prevent a dishonest invocation (D18, F2).
README.md workflow step 10 and the CLI Overview gate verdict row teach the bound form. examples/ is unchanged; no user-visible example surface.

Snapshot production, decided here. On gate verdict, src/gates/command.ts calls runReview for the named change with the same default severity threshold the CLI uses (warning when omitted; src/review/command.ts:56-59). command.ts maps every displayed finding onto the ReviewVerdictRecord, computes snapshotDigest from those findings, and passes that record into recordReviewVerdict, which persists each as a Finding child of the new Verdict: code, file, findingId, severity, ruleId, anchorOrHunkKey, message. snapshotDigest is SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of {changeId, findings sorted by (code, file, findingId) of those fields}. No timestamp enters the digest. Apply does not re-run review; it reads the persisted children. Re-running after archive is not the evidence.

Caller location, decided here because the ledger import is a cycle. src/review/core.ts:81 imports classifyApprovedArtifact and listGateDecisions from ../gates/ledger; runReview is :1439. Importing runReview into ledger.ts closes gates/ledger → review/core → gates/ledger. A new src/*.ts to break that cycle is refused (no-new-file Constraint). command.ts is the caller. Nothing under src/review/* imports gates/command (measured). command.ts:34 already imports ../review/outcomes, so the layering is established. Production review/*.ts has zero writeFileSync/mkdirSync (measured; tests excepted), so A35.2 and the five-file allowlist stay.
Unbound-pass refuse split, decided here. ledger.ts does not call runReview and cannot know that a review ran. What it still verifies on the record it was given is internal consistency: (a) outcome pass requires a snapshotDigest (an unbound record refuses persist); (b) snapshotDigest equals the canonical digest of those Finding children (command.ts computes; ledger.ts recomputes and refuses mismatch); (c) on pass, Ack findingIds match those children one-for-one. Extra, missing, or unknown ids, or a digest mismatch: recordReviewVerdict throws GraceCommandError and writes nothing. Those three checks are tamper-evidence of the persisted record (F2, D18). They do not prevent a caller from handing an empty finding set plus that empty-set digest; ledger cannot tell "runReview returned []" from "the caller invented []" without calling runReview.
What moves to command.ts is the "review ran" half: gate verdict always calls runReview before recordReviewVerdict; there is no argv to skip it. That is prevention of the default unbound CLI close, not prevention of a dishonest library call (the Goal already refuses that claim). evaluateApplyGate still reads persisted children and does not re-run review; its refuse set (unbound digest, digest mismatch, Ack mismatch, outcome fail) is the same tamper-evidence half.
This does not weaken the guarantee already scoped. An unbound pass is no longer the default successful close through ngrace gate verdict. Forging a bound pass by calling recordReviewVerdict with invented findings remains a visible library act, same class as D18.

Finding-set identity, decided here, because findingId is not change-scoped (src/review/core.ts:323-335). An Ack is valid only as the triple changeId plus snapshotDigest plus findingId against the newest Verdict on that same change. Code alone is forbidden (D18; review.write-evidence-outside-scope recurs). findingId alone is forbidden (same hash on a later bundle). Sorted path set without the digest is forbidden (a later review that adds a finding on a path already present would silently inherit the old Ack). The digest is what makes the set non-transferable across time and across bundles.

Pass recording, decided here. outcome pass requires argv token ack-finding once per persisted displayed finding, value equal to that findingId. Zero findings: no ack-finding flags, but the empty-set digest is still stored so the pass is bound to that empty finding set. Binding to "a review that ran" is the command.ts call, not a ledger inference from emptiness. Extra, missing, or unknown ids: recordReviewVerdict throws GraceCommandError, writes nothing. There is no ack-all flag. argv token note remains optional free text and is not the clearance mechanism; the findingId= note protocol in src/review/catalog.ts:226-232 is replaced by Ack children.

Fail recording, decided here. outcome fail: command.ts re-runs review, passes Finding children and the digest into recordReviewVerdict, and does not require Ack children. evaluateApplyGate refuses outcome fail. That narrows RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY D11 ("applied requires a recorded review verdict, not a clean one"; docs/plans/archive/RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY/decisions.md:733-742 and core.test.ts:332-334). Presence remains required. Cleanliness of findings remains not required: a pass with complete Acks of open findings still permits. Fail is the human reject and the switch to supersede, not a permitting close. unable-to-determine with reason host-capability-missing is unchanged and still uses gateFailOn (src/gates/core.ts:393-409). A bound pass is retroactive only for apply on active bundles after this writer ships. Archived applied bundles are not re-applied (D5.2: do not turn a legitimate historical close into an error).

Critical, decided here, is not a finding severity and is not a path class. Critical means the close would be a lie if it proceeded, and an Ack cannot make it true. Closed set: (1) pass with no snapshotDigest (unbound, including a pass that names no digest of an empty set); (2) snapshotDigest on the Verdict that does not match the canonical digest of its own Finding children; (3) an Ack whose findingId is not among those children, or whose digest does not equal the Verdict digest; (4) outcome fail. Those refuse apply and the operator switches to ngrace supersede. They are not acknowledgeable. (1)-(3) are tamper-evidence of the persisted record: ledger refuses them at persist, apply refuses them on read, neither re-runs review. (4) is apply prevention of a reject close (fail still records). The "review ran" half of unbound pass lives only on command.ts and is CLI-default prevention, not library-call prevention.
Not critical, and acknowledgeable: every live review.* finding about the work, including review.scope-outside-write-scope, review.write-evidence-outside-scope, review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated, review.confidently-wrong, review.test-assertion-weakened, and C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT's never-asked and mismatch codes. Acking them does not widen ObservedWriteScope. Rejecting them is outcome fail, then supersede. If the rejected finding is an undeclared write already on disk, the operator reverts those writes before supersede; that revert is not this bundle's verb.
The post-execution trap in the brief is the C-SUPERSEDE-VERB class: an undeclared forced write, already executed, on a release-surface file. Defining critical as "touches the release surface" would make that class unacknowledgeable and un-closeable without revert-then-supersede, with no honest pass path. That definition is refused here. That class is acknowledgeable. The operator may still reject it; that is a decision, not a critical classification.

Who records, decided here. F9.10.1: a declaration authored by the party under examination cannot be that examination's ground truth. The implementing executor must not invoke gate verdict. ngrace-execute rule 9 changes from "record with ngrace gate verdict" to: run ngrace review --change C-ID, report the findingIds, stop, and wait for the examining party to record the bound verdict. The examining party is a detached reviewer where the host allows it, otherwise the operator. ngrace-reviewer and the contract-reviewer role keep forming judgment and recording the bound verdict with ack-finding flags; they are not the executor. This is tamper-evidence, not enforcement (D18). A single actor with write access can still run review, copy the ids, and record pass. What changes is that an unbound pass is no longer the default successful close.
